notes: Same IW/id Tech 3 lineage as Call of Duty 2, so RCON is the Quake 3 connectionless dialect, NOT Valve Source RCON: an out-of-band UDP datagram carrying 'rcon <password> <command>' to the game port, answered by a 'print' packet. Hence flavour 'custom'. It shares the game port (net_port, default 28960 - the CubeCoders AMP template literally contains 'set net_port "28960"' and 'set rcon_password ""', and LinuxGSM's cod4server config passes +set net_port ${port} with port=28960); there is no separate port and no enable switch - setting a non-empty rcon_password turns it on - so enableSetting is null. playerId is the client/slot number in the first column of 'status'; BigBrotherBot issues 'status' through its q3a AbstractParser and parses the slot column. The slot is reassigned on every connection, so re-read 'status' immediately before kicking or banning. Name-based forms exist (kick <name>, onlykick <name>, banuser <name>, tempbanuser <name>); 'kick' needs the name typed with its colour codes (^1 etc.) - the silent-no-op case this dataset warns about - so the number-based clientkick/banclient are recorded, which is also what BigBrotherBot's cod4.py sends ('kick': 'clientkick %(cid)s', 'ban': 'banclient %(cid)s'; it keeps the name form separately as 'kickbyfullname': 'kick %(cid)s'). banclient writes the player's 32-hex-character GUID to ban.txt, created in the main or fs_game directory (zeroy CoD4 FAQ, patch 1.4 note). A live 'unbanuser <name>' exists (zeroy wiki, Gamesclan, and BigBrotherBot's 'unban': 'unbanuser %(name)s') but keys on player NAME, not the client number, so it cannot be expressed with the {playerId} token and is omitted rather than written wrongly. banList is omitted because no source found documents the ban.txt line format; a wrong lineIdPattern would silently leave bans in force. tempbanclient/tempbanuser take no duration argument - length comes from the sv_kickBanTime dvar (4Netplayers says so explicitly; the AMP template ships 'set sv_kickBanTime "300"') - so ban is the permanent form with no {duration}. motd is omitted, but not because scr_motd is mod-only: it is a stock CoD4 dvar and the CubeCoders AMP stock server.cfg sets it ('set scr_motd "^4Welcome to COD4!"'). It is omitted because it is a dvar set in config or via 'set', not a runtime message command, and changing it does not deliver a message to players already connected. The status GUID column is 32 hex characters here (BigBrotherBot's cod4.py _regPlayer uses [0-9a-f]+ and its embedded sample output shows 32-char ids), unlike the short numeric GUID matched by cod.py for CoD2, which is why playerParse differs between the two files; the regex was re-tested against that sample and matches every real line in it. Independence and coverage, checked source by source: status, clientkick, banclient and say are each carried by three separate lines - BigBrotherBot's cod4 parser source, the 4Netplayers wiki, and the Gamesclan hosting-KB lineage - and the zeroy Rcon Commands page adds a fourth for status/clientkick/banclient but does NOT document 'say'. serverinfo rests on two lines only, zeroy and the Gamesclan lineage; 4Netplayers does not list it. Lineage caution: the Gamesclan CoD4 page is byte-identical in wording to the anarchyrules CoD2 page ('Kicks a player by name from the server. (Must include Color Codes)'), and Pingperfect, fshost and MirzaLeka/COD4-Scripting repeat the same text, so that whole family counts as ONE source, not five. The zeroy Rcon Commands page is a generic cross-title page (it is filed under Call of Duty 7 and states the console commands are very similar in all CoD editions), so it corroborates but is not CoD4-specific.
